notes:
Copilot rewinds IN PLACE on the SAME session id — /undo (alias /rewind) ends in sessionTruncateEventsBeforeEventId, which truncates the session's own event history and rebuilds its projection; it never calls clearHistory, so no new session-state/<id>/ directory is minted (contrast 1-5 session-reset, where /clear DOES rotate the id). The spec therefore mirrors the claudecode in-place sibling, re-anchored onto this column's two-phase presession birth (proc-<PID> row first, then the real <session-id> once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt). The rewind ITSELF is asserted only as 'the session stays in ready': session.snapshot_rewind is emitEphemeral, so it is not persisted, and no state-changing event reaches the daemon. PROVISIONAL — whether the truncation physically shrinks events.jsonl is unverified (the truncate lives in the compressed Node-SEA native addon; the JS layer exposes only an append primitive). If it does shrink, the tailer's rotation/rewrite detection replays from byte 0 and the recording MAY show one extra working→ready blip between v2_turn_end and v3_turn_start; that blip is deliberately NOT asserted here, because the scenario requires only the arc. model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only auto and session.auto_mode_resolved routes per turn between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5.

RECORDED 2026-08-05 (CLI 1.0.78). TWO FACTS THIS CELL SETTLED, both from the transcript rather than from the bundle.

(1) THE REWIND IS IN PLACE, AND IT IS DESTRUCTIVE. events.jsonl is NOT append-only: rewinding to the checkpoint before turn 2 REWRITES the file and DELETES that turn's records. In this recording turn 2 ran normally (working 19:11:19.925 → ready 19:11:23.010) and afterwards its user.message and assistant.message are simply gone — all that survives is its orphaned system.message at 17:11:19.806, plus a session.info marker at 17:11:32.897. The session ID does NOT rotate (721807ad throughout), which is what separates rewind from /clear in cell 1-5: one mints a new session, the other truncates the existing one. This is the same shrinking-file hazard mistral-vibe's 2.19.1 `_overwrite_messages_sync` introduced, and the daemon survives it — the tailer keeps classifying correctly across the truncation and the following turn drives a clean working→ready.

(2) IT BROKE THE DRIVER, AND THAT IS WHY THIS CELL WAS FROZEN. The first attempt timed out with a complete, correct recording sitting behind it: three prompts were sent but the rewind erased one, so turn_count went DOWN to 2 against an EXPECTED_TURNS of 3 that only ever climbs, and wait_turn could never be satisfied again. wait_turn now absorbs a shrink into EXPECTED_TURNS.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED: the real session is born directly into working (commit 3cde4f8d), so session_birth and v1_turn_start are ONE phase. The rewind itself surfaces as a 1ms working→ready pair (19:11:33.006 → .007) — the in-place rewrite registers as one activity tick that immediately settles, since the rewound tail ends on a completed turn. Not user-visible, but the phases below name it rather than letting v3 silently bind to it.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
The first prompt materializes events.jsonl, so the real <session-id> session reconciles under a different id and is born DIRECTLY into working (commit 3cde4f8d)
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)
assistant.turn_end settles the first turn back to ready. This turn is the checkpoint the rewind returns to, and it is the one that SURVIVES the rewrite
The second prompt drives ready → working on the same session. Everything this turn writes is erased a few seconds later — the daemon still has to track it correctly while it is happening

The second turn settles back to ready and HOLDS there — the state the rewind is taken from. /undo is driven through the TUI picker, which writes nothing to the transcript until it commits, so the session must not churn while the user is choosing a checkpoint
The rewind commits: events.jsonl is rewritten in place, turn 2's records are deleted, and the resulting file change registers as one activity tick

Spec: 'Session row reflects the rewound state with state ready'. It settles immediately — the rewound tail ends on turn 1's completed turn_end — so the rewind is not mistaken for agent work. Crucially the session id is UNCHANGED: a rewind truncates the session, it does not mint a new one (contrast 1-5, where /clear does)

Spec: 'Subsequent turns start cleanly from the rewound point: ready → working'. The third prompt drives the SAME session — proof the tailer re-synchronised against a file that shrank under it rather than wedging on a stale offset
The third turn completes back to ready on the same session; final state ready, and the session never entered waiting
